_comment: BLOCKS-PER-STAGE point: n_stages 1, blocks_per_stage 1, max_loops 16 = 16 block applications/token.
WHAT THIS AXIS IS. The stages<->width frontier varied n_stages with
blocks_per_stage pinned at 1, so two things moved together: how many
distinct parameter sets the model has, AND where in the sequence the
repetition happens. At n_stages=1 the loop is unambiguously over the whole
block stack -- the blocks pass, then the stack passes again -- so this
sweep varies only the grouping.
1 stage x 1 block(s) x 16 loop(s) = 16 block applications
GATE STRUCTURE IS THE PART THAT IS NOT INTERCHANGEABLE WITH n_stAGES.
param_count scales the encoder stack by n_stages * blocks_per_stage, but the
halting gates scale by n_stages ALONE. So this model has ONE gate watching
1 blocks, where frontier s01l16 had 16 gates watching 1 block each.
This is the 'global ACT over the stack' ablation named in LoopedConfig's
own doc comment. Roles will read UNREADABLE/UNKNOWN here by construction --
one stage means there are no stage roles to differentiate. That is expected
and is not a failure of the run.
Also note d_model FALLS as blocks_per_stage rises, because a fixed parameter
budget split across more distinct blocks leaves each one narrower. That is
the same width/reuse trade the frontier had, running the other way, and it
is not removable at fixed parameters. Read this axis as 'grouping at fixed
budget', not as 'reuse with width held constant' -- for the latter, see the
fixed-width points.
Config from examples/param_match.rs (fourth argument = blocks_per_stage):
cargo run --example param_match -- 16 1 492418 1
Rung: same-rule (subst-fst-fixed, k_set [0], k0_rate 1.0).
auto_batch FALSE, batch_size 6, matching the clean frontier pass.
Run:
cargo run --example scaling_sweep -- \
research/experiments/stack-bps01x16.json depth gpu 16 \
